headline: 624 detained in Cumilla on suspicion of teenage gang involvement
summary: Police conducted simultaneous raids across 18 police stations in the district to curb criminal activities among youths.
details: Police have detained 624 people in Cumilla on suspicion of involvement in teenage gangs. The operation was carried out across all 18 police station jurisdictions in the district on Wednesday night.
Cumilla Additional Superintendent of Police Lutfur Rahman stated that the detainees are being questioned and legal action will be taken after verifying the information.

The operation was ordered by Superintendent of Police Md Anisuzzaman following reports of teenagers involved in various criminal activities and complaints from residents about harassment by youth groups.
The crackdown on teenage gang activity has gained renewed focus following the killing of Ishayat Shahriar Apratim, a 13-year-old son of a Cumilla University teacher.
During the operation, 17 detainees reportedly escaped from a room at Daudkandi Police Station by breaking down a door due to overcrowding.
Police officials confirmed that the escapees were quickly recaptured by local people and brought back to the station.

headline_marked: PM Tarique Rahman [[meets Iranian President]] to discuss Middle East tensions
headline: PM Tarique Rahman meets Iranian President to discuss Middle East tensions
summary: The Prime Minister sought Iran's cooperation for the safe movement of Bangladeshi vessels and containers through the Strait of Hormuz.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman met with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian on the sidelines of the 81st UN General Assembly in New York.
The leaders discussed the ongoing Middle East conflict and the safety of Bangladeshi expatriate workers and professionals in the region.
The Prime Minister called for an early resolution of the conflict through diplomacy, stressing its potential impact on Bangladesh's energy security and trade.
Bangladesh specifically sought Iran's cooperation in facilitating the safe movement of Bangladeshi vessels and containers through the Strait of Hormuz as the situation improves.
State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir stated that Bangladesh maintains a neutral position and is prepared to play a constructive role in promoting peace and stability.
The meeting also focused on the well-being of the expatriate population and the broader implications of regional instability on international peace.
caption:
PM Tarique Rahman meets Iranian President in New York to discuss Middle East tensions and the safety of Bangladeshi workers.

Prime Minister Tarique Rahman met with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian on the sidelines of the 81st UN General Assembly in New York.

The leaders discussed the ongoing Middle East conflict and the safety of Bangladeshi expatriate workers and professionals in the region.

The Prime Minister called for an early resolution of the conflict through diplomacy, stressing its potential impact on Bangladesh's energy security and trade.

Bangladesh specifically sought Iran's cooperation in facilitating the safe movement of Bangladeshi vessels and containers through the Strait of Hormuz as the situation improves.

State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir stated that Bangladesh maintains a neutral position and is prepared to play a constructive role in promoting peace and stability.

The meeting also focused on the well-being of the expatriate population and the broader implications of regional instability on international peace.
